query: Onboarding data: users who add a payment method in their first session convert to paid within 30 days at 41%, against 9% for users who don't. About 120k signups a month, 22% add a payment method in session one, ARPU is $18 a month. The PM wants to make the payment-method step mandatory in onboarding and needs the revenue opportunity for Thursday's roadmap review. Our prior store is in priors.jsonl. Size it for me.
expected_behavior: Does not present the 32-point gap times the non-adders (about $540k a month) as the opportunity; if it computes it, it labels it the ceiling and nothing more. Names self-selection: users who add a card in session one had already decided to pay. Reads the prior store: five onboarding tests on paid_conversion_30d, effects from -0.1pp to +0.9pp with a mean around +0.3pp and a dismissible card prompt worth +0.3pp in July, so the anchored estimate is on the order of a few hundred extra payers a month (0.3pp of 120k is about 360, roughly $6k a month), two orders of magnitude under the ceiling, with +0.9pp (about 1,100 payers) as the most any onboarding change has produced. Computes or states the MDE at 120k signups a month (about 0.5pp absolute over six weeks) and concludes a test is worth funding because the largest recorded effect clears it, routing to designing-experiments with signups as a guardrail since a mandatory step also loses people. Hands back the three numbers side by side with the assumptions as line items. Without the skill, the model typically produces the $540k figure with a caveat, proposes an A/B test, and ignores or merely mentions the prior store rather than anchoring on it.
